bpj.kirish: Smart3D hands the project to Bazis-Mebelshchik as a .bpj file, and Bazis itself writes the .b3d — 3 steps:
bpj.q1: In Bazis-Mebelshchik, open a new empty model and run the BazisUniversalImport.js script.
bpj.q2: In the script, press «BPJ Import» and choose the .bpj file downloaded here.
bpj.q3: When the model appears: Файл → «Сохранить как…» → .b3d.
bpj.sinov: TEST — not yet checked in real Bazis. The file contains the boards (parts, holes, edging); the hardware list is not included yet, and there is no room.
b3d.kirish: Smart3D gives the project as a ready Bazis-Mebelshchik file (.b3d) — 3 steps:
b3d.q1: Download the file (button below) and open Bazis-Mebelshchik.
b3d.q3: Compare modules, panel count, sizes and material with the Smart3D list. If it will not open or differs — send the error code and the file.
b3d.sinov: TEST — the file is checked inside Smart3D (reading it back gives the same panel count, sizes, material and position), but opening it in real Bazis has not been tried yet. The file has modules, board parts (size, position, material, edge band) and a fittings list; no drill holes and no 3D fitting shapes.
altendorf.kirish: The file for the Altendorf saw (.gibcut) is created in GibLab. Path: Smart3D → GibLab (.project) → GibLab → Altendorf.
altendorf.q1: Download the GibLab (.project) file with the button below.
altendorf.q2: Open this .project in GibLab — GibLab optimises the cutting itself.
altendorf.q3: GibLab exports the Altendorf saw file (.gibcut) and it goes to the machine.
altendorf.eslatma: Smart3D does not write .gibcut: it is GibLab's closed format (the cutting map is encrypted). For a printed text plan use Files → «Cutting plan (text)».
